analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md, in the base-side region at about line 2115 and the head-side region at about lines 2115-2131. It replaces a sentence fragment with a description of a new offline test suite for the Model Requant Upload workflow (python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/models). The new text states that the suite needs no network and no credentials, and that Release Integrity also runs it. It lists claims about the workflow's design: a secret-free preflight, a job in the prod environment, master-only runs, and R2 key set checks. It also claims the upload holds only the chosen key set, tools are pinned by hash, and a selftest runs before any secret is read. No code, workflow, key handling, runtime or trust-boundary behavior changes in this diff, so none of the provider, coordinator, cache (T-041) or attestation threat entries is affected. I found no new attack surface and no invalidated assumption.

The new documentation describes security-relevant controls (prod environment gating, master-only, hash-pinned tools, secret-free preflight). The workflow, scripts/models tests and requant.py are not in the supplied evidence, so the accuracy of these claims is unverified. That is a documentation-accuracy question for whoever reviews the workflow files themselves, not a finding here. The base excerpts from lines 1807-2730 are unchanged context and also introduce no changes. The Model Requant Upload workflow is not covered by the retained threat model scope, which excludes backend and publication infrastructure.
